shortDescription: Chicago Board of Trade corn futures closed lower after a choppy trading session on Tuesday as traders positioned ahead of Friday's widely anticipated U.S. Department of Agriculture supply and demand report.

children: Chicago Board of Trade corn futures closed lower after a choppy trading session on Tuesday as traders positioned ahead of Friday's widely anticipated U.S. Department of Agriculture supply and demand report.
Expectations for poor yields in the U.S. Corn Belt have kept a floor on corn futures.
Weather in the U.S. Midwest will largely remain warmer and drier in the coming weeks, limiting harvest slowdowns and frost risks, according to forecaster Commodity Weather Group.

But the firm raised its corn production forecast to 16.207 billion bushels, from 16.160 billion previously. StoneX said it calculated production using acreage figures from the U.S. Department of Agriculture, which raised its national corn acreage estimate on August 12.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture on Friday reported that 5% of the U.S. corn crop had been harvested, with 56% of the crop in good-excellent condition.
